# Base44 games: Three.js: assets models textures

<assets_models_textures>
Use this when loading textures or 3D models, animating loaded models, or generating surfaces procedurally.

<textures>
- `useTexture` is suspense-aware; the game image tools produce URLs that load straight into it. Keep generated URLs in `src/game/config.js`.
- Tiling a texture across a large ground plane: set `wrapS`/`wrapT` to `THREE.RepeatWrapping` and a `repeat` count. Pixel-art crispness: `magFilter = THREE.NearestFilter`. Color textures that look washed out: set `colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace` (the old `.encoding`/`sRGBEncoding` API is gone — never emit it).
- Procedural surfaces (stripes, grids, text-on-surface): draw a small offscreen 2D canvas once (memoized, never per frame) and wrap it in `THREE.CanvasTexture`.
</textures>

<models>
- `useGLTF` loads a model (suspends); mount its `scene` with `<primitive object={...} />`. A loaded GLTF scene can be mounted only ONCE — render additional copies with drei `<Clone object={...} />`.
- Animations: `useAnimations(animations, groupRef)` exposes `actions`; crossfade states on gameplay events by fading out the current action and `reset().fadeIn().play()` on the next. Action names come from the file — log the keys of `actions` when unsure.
- Loaded models don't cast shadows by default: traverse the scene once and set `castShadow` on each mesh.
- Loaders cache by URL — using the same URL in ten components fetches once. Start downloads early with `useGLTF.preload`/`useTexture.preload` at module scope; drei `<Preload all />` inside the Canvas uploads everything to the GPU up front, killing first-encounter hitches.
</models>

<sourcing>
Only reference model/texture URLs that actually exist (uploaded by the user or generated by the image tools) — there is no built-in asset library, and hallucinated URLs render nothing. When no model exists, build characters/props from primitives composed in a `<group>` (see the visuals guidance) — it looks intentional and ships now.
</sourcing>
</assets_models_textures>
